findings.summary: Fresh browser sessions can remain a blank shell, blocking discovery and reading.
findings.evidence: Six raw-CDP captures across home, title, chapter and collection stayed at a uniform #181a1c background after 12 seconds; the 12-second probe found 26 nodes, zero links, zero controls and no body text. Lighthouse did render the homepage in a separate run, proving an intermittent/runtime-dependent boot failure rather than intentional emptiness.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the server-rendered shell contain the core listing/detail content and diagnose the client bootstrap race. Do not remove usable content during hydration; retain a functional fallback if enhancement fails.

findings.summary: The failed bootstrap presents no loading, error, retry or recovery state.
findings.evidence: The persistent blank captures and content probe show no status text or interactive control after 12 seconds.
findings.suggestedFix: Render a durable loading state immediately, catch bootstrap/data failures, and replace it with an actionable error panel containing Retry and a plain-link route to core content.

findings.summary: Core content is not available without successful JavaScript execution.
findings.evidence: Discoverability fetched 393,664 bytes of raw homepage HTML but extracted only 35 text characters and five content tokens; title raw HTML likewise exposed 39 text characters/five tokens. Both crawler screenshots are blank, while data is serialized inside scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render meaningful headings, links, cover metadata and chapter links as HTML. Hydrate those nodes progressively instead of requiring JavaScript to create the entire experience.

findings.summary: Runtime behavior is inconsistent across clean Chrome sessions.
findings.evidence: Raw-CDP sessions repeatedly rendered no UI, while Lighthouse rendered the homepage and recorded content. This session-dependent result indicates fragile initialization or bot/challenge interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Instrument bootstrap failures, make initialization idempotent, and ensure Cloudflare/challenge code cannot leave the app root empty. Preserve server content until the client is ready.

findings.summary: The site forces its dark palette even when the OS requests light mode.
findings.evidence: The light-preference probe matched prefers-color-scheme: light but computed body colors remained rgb(24,26,28) on rgb(212,212,212); the static scan found no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and derive surfaces/text from system-aware custom properties or light-dark(), while retaining an explicit user override if desired.

findings.summary: No reduced-motion adaptation is implemented in shipped CSS.
findings.evidence: The static CSS/JS scan found no prefers-reduced-motion handling. The page contains carousels and motion-capable UI in the successful Lighthouse render.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce layer that removes non-essential transitions, auto-advance and smooth scrolling while preserving state feedback.

findings.summary: No high-contrast or forced-colors adaptation is present.
findings.evidence: The static scan found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules, and Lighthouse separately found contrast failures in the rendered UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Use system colors/forced-color-adjust carefully for controls and add a prefers-contrast treatment that strengthens essential boundaries and text.

findings.summary: Route and state swaps do not use the View Transitions API.
findings.evidence: The shipped application assets contained no startViewTransition usage, despite a route-heavy browse, detail and reader experience.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-document view transitions around SPA route/state commits, with stable view-transition-name values and reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: The long listing UI lacks declarative scroll-state-aware navigation treatment.
findings.evidence: The static scan found scroll-snap but no scroll-driven timeline or scroll-state/container-query implementation; the successful screenshot shows a dense scroll surface with fixed top navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS scroll-state queries or a lightweight declarative progress/affordance treatment to show scroll position and compact persistent chrome.

findings.summary: Components rely on global layout rules rather than container queries.
findings.evidence: The shipped CSS contained no @container or container-type despite reusable comic-card/carousel components.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable card/list regions containment and adapt card density/type within @container rules, retaining viewport fallbacks.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is far outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 7.1 seconds (score 0.05), FCP 2.9 seconds and time to interactive 7.2 seconds.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize discovery of the first meaningful card/hero, server-render it, preload only its critical asset, and defer non-critical scripts and below-fold work.

findings.summary: Render-blocking styles and dependency chains delay useful content.
findings.evidence: HAR identified four very-high-priority parser-inserted stylesheets plus the application script as candidates; Lighthouse estimated 900 ms render-blocking savings and the document itself took about 995 ms. DOM confirms stylesheets are in the head and the main script has no async/defer/module attribute.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline minimal critical CSS, consolidate/remove duplicate font imports, defer non-critical CSS, and load the bootstrap script with module/defer semantics after preserving server content.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused CSS and JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 44 KiB unused CSS and 117 KiB unused JavaScript; HAR transferred 248,355 bytes of scripts before the core UI reliably appeared.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by route, remove duplicate/unused vendor code, and conditionally import collection, reader and account features.

findings.summary: Rendered controls include links without names and visible labels that do not match accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed link-name and label-content-name-mismatch; its accessibility score was 0.87.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every icon-only link a discernible name, align aria-label text with visible labels, and verify the accessibility tree for carousel and card actions.

findings.summary: Some foreground/background pairs fail minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the color-contrast audit in the rendered homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust muted text, icon and control tokens to meet WCAG AA in the dark theme and re-test all interactive states.

findings.summary: Heading hierarchy is not sequential.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed heading-order on the rendered homepage; raw-CDP failure states provide no focusable recovery control at all.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a single page h1 followed by level-2 section headings without skipped levels, and move focus to an announced recovery state when bootstrap fails.

findings.summary: The viewport explicitly disables user zoom.
findings.evidence: The live viewport meta is width=device-width, initial-scale=1, user-scalable=no; Lighthouse failed meta-viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no and do not cap maximum-scale. Test at 200% and 400% zoom and at 320 CSS px reflow.

findings.summary: Cloudflare challenge code invokes deprecated browser APIs.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported three deprecation warnings from /cdn-cgi/challenge-platform/scripts/jsd/main.js, including deprecated Shared Storage, persistent storage and Protected Audience APIs.
findings.suggestedFix: Update or reconfigure the challenge integration and verify that injected edge scripts no longer trigger deprecated APIs.

findings.summary: Public pages omit canonical URLs and expose no sitemap at /sitemap.xml.
findings.evidence: Raw homepage and title HTML contain no rel=canonical; /sitemap.xml returns an HTML 404 page. Robots is syntactically valid but includes multiple bot-specific Disallow rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a real XML sitemap, add self-referential canonicals to indexable templates, and keep robots directives consistent with intended indexing.

findings.summary: Comic detail pages lack structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: The representative title HTML has a descriptive title/meta description but no JSON-LD, canonical or hreflang.
findings.suggestedFix: Add schema.org ComicStory/CreativeWork JSON-LD matching visible title, image, creator and chapter data, plus complete Open Graph/Twitter metadata.

findings.summary: Core security response headers are missing.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirmed HTTPS but found no CSP, HSTS or X-Content-Type-Options.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy an enforcing nonce/hash-based CSP, HSTS with an appropriate max-age, and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Test challenge and asset paths before rollout.

findings.summary: Clickjacking, referrer and permissions defenses are not configured.
findings.evidence: No CSP frame-ancestors, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Set frame-ancestors in CSP, a strict-origin-when-cross-origin (or stricter) Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: The install manifest has no active service worker/offline fallback.
findings.evidence: The manifest declares standalone display/start_url, but navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations() returned an empty list.
findings.suggestedFix: Register a scoped service worker, precache the app shell and provide an explicit offline page; ensure stale comic metadata is labelled rather than presented as fresh.

findings.summary: A failed client load degrades to an unlabelled blank screen.
findings.evidence: Repeated fresh sessions are direct network/runtime failure-state evidence: no spinner, timeout, error copy, retry or fallback links appear by 12 seconds.
findings.suggestedFix: Add timeout-aware fetch/bootstrap boundaries and an accessible retry/offline state that preserves server-rendered links.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes relative to displayed size.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 671 KiB image-delivery savings on the successfully rendered homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive AVIF/WebP sources sized to card slots, include width/height, and prioritize only the above-fold candidate.
